content: Voriconazole significantly interacts with various drugs by altering their metabolism through hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Below are the detailed interactions and recommendations for coadministration: 1. Avapritinib: Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If unavoidable, consider alternative drugs. 2. Axitinib: Voriconazole increases axitinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is necessary, reduce the axitinib dose by 50%. 3. Bedaquiline: Voriconazole increases bedaquiline levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors for more than 14 consecutive days unless the benefits outweigh the risks. 4. Bosutinib: Voriconazole increases bosutinib levels approximately fivefold. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 5. Brigatinib: Voriconazole increases brigatinib levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce the brigatinib dose by 50%. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the inhibitor. 6. Bromocriptine: Voriconazole increases bromocriptine levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 7. Buprenorphine: Voriconazole increases buprenorphine levels and both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. This applies to all buprenorphine formulations (buccal, subdermal implant, transdermal, long-acting injection). 8. Butabarbital and Butalbital: These drugs decrease voriconazole levels by increasing its metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated. 9. Cabazitaxel: Voriconazole increases cabazitaxel levels. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 10. Cabozantinib: Voriconazole increases cabozantinib levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is required, reduce the cabozantinib dose (40 mg/day for Cometriq or 20 mg/day for Cabometyx). Resume the previous dose 2–3 days after discontinuing the inhibitor. 11. Capivasertib: Voriconazole increases capivasertib levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the capivasertib dose and monitor for adverse effects. 12. Ceritinib: Voriconazole increases ceritinib levels, and both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 13. Chloroquine: Voriconazole increases chloroquine levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 14. Citalopram: Both voriconazole and citalopram prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 15. Clarithromycin: Clarithromycin increases voriconazole levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 16. Clopidogrel: Voriconazole decreases clopidogrel efficacy by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 17. Clozapine: Both voriconazole and clozapine prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 18. Colchicine: Voriconazole increases colchicine levels. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If necessary, reduce the colchicine dose or frequency as per prescribing information. Coadministration is contraindicated in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. 19. Conivaptan: Conivaptan increases voriconazole levels. Coadministration is contraindicated. 20. Copanlisib: Voriconazole increases copanlisib levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the copanlisib dose to 45 mg. 21. Crizotinib: Both voriconazole and crizotinib prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 22. Dabrafenib: Voriconazole increases dabrafenib levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 23. Daridorexant: Voriconazole increases daridorexant levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 24. Darunavir: Darunavir increases voriconazole levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 25. Desflurane: Both voriconazole and desflurane prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 26. Disopyramide: Both voriconazole and disopyramide prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 27. Doxepin Cream: Voriconazole increases doxepin cream levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 28. Dronedarone: Voriconazole increases dronedarone levels. Coadministration is contraindicated. 29. Efavirenz: Both voriconazole and efavirenz prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 30. Elacestrant: Voriconazole increases elacestrant levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 31. Eliglustat: Both voriconazole and eliglustat prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 32. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF: Voriconazole increases the levels of this combination. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 33. Encorafenib: Voriconazole increases encorafenib levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the encorafenib dose to one-third of the original dose. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the inhibitor for 3–5 elimination half-lives. 34. Entrectinib: Both voriconazole and entrectinib prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 35. Enzalutamide: Voriconazole increases enzalutamide levels. Coadministration is contraindicated. 36. Erdafitinib: Voriconazole increases erdafitinib levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, monitor closely for adverse reactions and consider dose adjustments. 37. Eribulin: Both voriconazole and eribulin prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 38. Erythromycin (Base, Ethylsuccinate, Lactobionate, Stearate): Voriconazole increases erythromycin levels. Coadministration is contraindicated. 39. Etravirine: Voriconazole increases etravirine levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 40. Everolimus: Voriconazole increases everolimus levels. Coadministration is contraindicated. 41. Fedratinib: Voriconazole increases fedratinib levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the fedratinib dose to 200 mg/day. 42. Fentanyl (Intranasal, Transdermal, Transmucosal): Voriconazole increases fentanyl levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, monitor for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust the fentanyl dose as needed. 43. Fexinidazole: Voriconazole decreases fexinidazole levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. 44. Fluoxetine: Fluoxetine increases voriconazole levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 45. Fluticasone (Intranasal): Voriconazole increases fluticasone levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Monitor for signs of high corticosteroid concentrations. 46. Fosamprenavir: Both voriconazole and fosamprenavir increase each other's levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 47. Fosphenytoin: Fosphenytoin decreases voriconazole levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 48. Gilteritinib: Voriconazole increases gilteritinib levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, monitor for gilteritinib-related adverse effects. 49. Givinostat: Both voriconazole and givinostat prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, obtain ECGs and monitor QTc interval changes. 50. Glasdegib: Voriconazole increases glasdegib levels, and both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 51. Hydroxychloroquine Sulfate: Both voriconazole and hydroxychloroquine prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 52. Ibrutinib: Voriconazole increases ibrutinib levels. Reduce the ibrutinib dose when coadministered with voriconazole. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the inhibitor. 53. Ibutilide: Both voriconazole and ibutilide prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 54. Idelalisib: Voriconazole increases idelalisib levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, monitor for idelalisib toxicity and adjust the dose as needed. 55. Indapamide: Both voriconazole and indapamide prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 56. Indinavir: Voriconazole increases indinavir levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug.
